ctor.rationale: `base(1, CardType.Attack, CardRarity.Common, TargetType.AnyEnemy)` (MoltenFist.cs:27-30) == cost 1 / ATTACK / COMMON / ANY_ENEMY.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `new DamageVar(10m, ValueProp.Move)` (MoltenFist.cs:23) == `_damage = 10`, powered on both sides.

OnPlay.rationale: This is the one card in the family where the liveness guard is FAITHFUL rather than a divergence, because C# writes it explicitly: `int num = (cardPlay.Target.IsAlive ? cardPlay.Target.GetPowerAmount<VulnerablePower>() : 0); if (num > 0) await PowerCmd.Apply<VulnerablePower>(...)` (MoltenFist.cs:38-42) == `if not target.is_gone and "vulnerable" in target.powers: vuln = ...; if vuln > 0: PowerCmd.apply(...)`. C#'s own `IsAlive` test is what the sim's `is_gone` mirrors, so unlike card/bash, card/break, card/fight_me, card/mangle and card/mad_science this card carries NO CanReceivePowers finding. The doubling amount is right too -- both sides read the target's CURRENT Vulnerable after the attack and apply that much again. Presentation, folded in: WithHitFx, ExtraRunAssetPaths and the Vulnerable hover tip.

guards.what: the sim's `is_gone` is `is_dead or escaped` where C#'s `IsAlive` tests only HP (creatures.py:44-46)
guards.rationale: The extra `escaped` term can only make the sim MORE conservative, and an escaped creature has been removed from C#'s Enemies list anyway (CreatureCmd.Escape, CreatureCmd.cs:579-603), so C# would also find no target. Same outcome.
